gaps: No Skid Row / DTLA / LAPD Central Division-specific counts for e-bike, moped or motorcycle theft or commercial burglary were found; the Crosstown analysis names University Park and Venice as top neighborhoods and does not mention Downtown. Answering this requires a direct query of the LAPD NIBRS open dataset by reporting district around 768 Ceres Ave.
No 2025 or 2026 LA motorized-device theft totals surfaced (Crosstown coverage ends Dec 2024).
No LA-specific breakdown by vehicle tier (e-bike vs moped vs motorcycle); NICB motorcycle theft data and LAPD vehicle-theft codes for motorcycles/mopeds were not searched in this pass.

No operator-disclosed fleet theft or non-return percentage beyond Whizz's unverified marketing claim (<1% stolen, 94% recovered); Zoomo, Lime, Bird do not publish fleet-wide loss rates. Lime's May 2026 S-1 on EDGAR was not read and may contain vehicle-loss or depreciation disclosures.

No named commercial insurer, MGA or broker writing e-bike / e-moped rental-fleet property or theft coverage in California was identified, and no premium, deductible or lithium-battery exclusion language was obtained. Only personal-lines (Velosurance) and broker blogs were found.
No Reddit r/smallbusiness, r/ebikes or operator-interview threads on renter fraud / non-return were surfaced by search; needs targeted site:reddit.com queries.
No Bike Index Los Angeles city-level counts or 529 Garage LA data found; only national figures.
GPS tracker pricing found is consumer/retail (Monimoto, Invoxia, Spytec); fleet IoT vendors (OMNI, PowUnity) are quote-based with no public pricing. No immobilizer-specific pricing.
Security-guard and camera figures are vendor marketing ranges, not quotes for an 8,443 sqft DTLA warehouse; bad-debt / collections benchmarks for rider subscriptions were not found.
must_ask_hmp: Actual SF theft, non-return and unrecovered-loss rates per month by tier (e-bike, moped, motorcycle) on the ~100 rented vehicles and ~300+ battery subscriptions, and the GPS recovery rate.

Current SF insurance program: carrier(s), coverage types (property/inland marine for fleet, garagekeepers, general liability, product liability), premium, deductibles, any lithium battery or rental exclusions, and whether the carrier will extend to an LA location.
Existing anti-theft stack and cost: GPS/immobilizer hardware installed per vehicle, telematics subscription per unit per month, lock policy.
Deposit, ID, credit-check and payment-verification policy used in SF, deposit amounts by tier, and the bad-debt / charge-off rate on rentals and battery subscriptions.
History of break-ins, burglaries or attempted theft at the SF facility and current site-security spend (alarm, cameras, guards).
Whether SF rental vehicles are UL 2849 / EN 15194 certified (relevant to SB 1271 rental prohibition from Jan 1, 2028 and to insurability).
surprises: Crosstown's analysis of LAPD motorized-device theft data (2020-2024) does not list Downtown or Skid Row among top neighborhoods; University Park (USC, 206 reports) and Venice (95) lead. This does not confirm the CONTEXT assumption that the Skid Row edge is the city's theft epicenter for e-bikes, though under-reporting there is plausible.

Whizz publicly claims less than 1% of its rental e-bikes are stolen and 94% of stolen bikes are recovered, which if true is far lower than the loss levels implied by the CONTEXT's 'major concern' framing (claim is marketing, unaudited).

Bird's early investor communications reportedly conceded theft/vandalism losses were 'underestimated by a serious multiple' (29-day lifespan vs 200+ planned), a cautionary datapoint for dockless-style models, though HMP's assigned-renter model differs.

California SB 1271 phase 2 (Jan 1, 2028) bars renting out e-bikes, chargers or batteries not tested to UL 2849 / EN 15194, a regulatory constraint on rental-fleet vehicle choice and insurability that was not in the CONTEXT.
Lime filed an S-1 in May 2026, so a public micromobility loss-rate/risk-factor source now exists on EDGAR that did not before.
